scope: Theorem 4.9 (Marked component expansion) of the manuscript “Hard-sphere fluctuations on the regular Boltzmann lifespan” (preprints/Hard-sphere-fluctuations-on-the-regular-Boltzmann-lifespan-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 364 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e294d8e5097f8d0e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 23. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Choose Γ and then L as above. These choices are independent of the moment order and the fixed observation list. On this single pasted dynamics the following statements hold. (i) The factorial hierarchy with any fixed finite list of records has the finite componentwise expan- sion (4.17), with the variation error (4.22). Its independent inputs are the gi in Proposition 4.5; its label weights, continuations, and record projections are those of Lemmas 4.6 and 4.7. (ii) At each fixed final order h, the actual normalized marked factorial cumulant cϵ h is the sum of retained globally connected diagrams, plus an error of total variation at most Che−cΛL . A nontrivial initial cumulant block is part of this connectivity. Dummy links are not. (iii) For any fixed accuracy power P, one can choose a constant K after the observation list and h such that all remaining retained diagrams with ρ > K have summed absolute variation at most ϵP . At ρ ≤ K the original fresh-label factorials satisfy (4.21). Neither increasing K nor increasing a fixed moment order changes the exponential base per ordinary atom in the preceding estimates.
